laneNotes: Five families assigned, five rows returned, all five stopped at the claim gate before anything was read.
Every one refuses with ALREADY_RELEASED. The grants are held by PF14 and marked released; the ledger's releases[] log records lane PF04 as the releaser, within a 0.3-second window on 2026-09-01.
None of the five has an overlay directory and none appears in any lane's rows.json, so five families were released without being built. That is a finding for whoever owns the dispatch and the ledger.
This lane wrote nothing for any of them and did not reopen a single grant.
grantsNothing: A built family is a built family. It is not verified, not approved, not sellable, and this lane issues no verdict on its own packets.

rows.rasterNote: Rendered locally through scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs on a calibrated Chromium (residual 0.5px, 2.667 px/pt) as this lane's own build check, and every raster PNG was deleted after measuring. A local raster is not central acceptance: the family returns BUILT_RASTER_PENDING and the hashes above are what the central raster acceptance binds.
rows.writeProof: byte-level. Each saved fixture is re-opened, its page content streams are decompressed, the streams the source already carried are excluded, and every remaining hex-encoded show-text operator is decoded with the position matrix that precedes it. A declared write that is not readable at its declared coordinates in the output bytes stops the build; ink in an added stream that no declared write accounts for is counted against nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes.
findings: Both official-form identities this family names resolve to ONE two-page binary. The custody reconciliation resolves them on first-hand document text: the Certification of Service is the section heading printed on page 2 of the application itself. The receipt records two source rows against one file and names the page each component occupies rather than implying a second file that does not exist.

The two Read Before Signing boxes are left unmarked. The form prints 'Please check each statement below after you have read it', which is an act of the person filing; marking them would assert that somebody had read something this build cannot know they read.

The two numbered items ARE the statutory elements of the section 123.47(9) route, so both are marked as route determinations and the conviction date is written. The application therefore states which route it proceeds under rather than asking the participant.

Every field of the certification of service is blank, including the certifier's own printed name which this packet holds, because a certificate of mailing completed before the mailing happened would be false. The recipient's name, address, city, state and ZIP are carried as disclosed required-before-filing items.

The caption's second plaintiff line ('State of Iowa or ______') is carried and disclosed rather than left as an unaccounted printed rule: a section 123.47 charge may be prosecuted by a city under its own ordinance, the platform holds no prosecuting-entity name, and inventing a city would put a false plaintiff on a filing sworn under penalty of perjury.

rows.writeProof: flat overlay through scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs. Every value is drawn at an anchor measured against this exact binary, every option mark is two diagonal strokes inset inside the court's own stroked box, and the build refuses the fixture if any anchor it claims was refused or any selection was not marked. No new box is ever drawn and the court's boxes are never redrawn.
findings: This family carries two routes on ONE court form and each route IS an option the form prints: or_arrest_no_charges (ORS 137.225(1)(c)) marks Option 3, or_dismissed_charge (ORS 137.225(1)(d)) marks Option 2. Each route is rendered with its own canonical and boundary fixture and the two motions are carried as separate document identities, so one route's write is never read against the other route's refusal.

The form prints '(leave blank if no court case)' beside the Case No. line. On or_arrest_no_charges the case-number slot is refused with that printed instruction as its named route condition and no case number is carried in that route's fixtures at all; on or_dismissed_charge the case number is written.

FINDING FOR THE OWNER: the packet-set manifest names a REQUIRED proposed_order component on both routes and assigns it to this same OR-OJD-ADULT-SET-ASIDE-PACKET binary. That binary contains a Motion, a Declaration of Eligibility and a Certificate of Mailing and no proposed order, and the Oregon corpus holds no order form at all. No order is drafted here, because an order is the court's act; the packet, the participant instructions and the composed filing instructions all say in terms that no proposed order is enclosed, and it is raised as a counsel question.

The option geometry records 10 of the 14 checkbox-shaped boxes it found: three options and seven declaration statements. The four it does not record are Option 1's two sub-elections and the two 'additional page' boxes. Option 1's sub-elections are off-route on both routes; the additional-page boxes are not marked because no committed measurement gives their coordinates and this build authors no coordinate.

The last three declaration boxes are printed under 'If you selected Option 1 above', so on both routes they are refused with that printed sentence as the named route condition rather than carried as elections the participant is expected to make.

The Phone column on the page-5 contact line is the court's own 34 points and no phone number fits it at the minimum readable machine font, so the phone is a disclosed required-before-filing item written by hand and the anchor is never offered to the renderer.

laneGate.note: Run without --codex-cloud and without --minimum-captain-sha: this lane is a git worktree on a browser-equipped container, not a Codex Cloud task.

firstRun.why: The container setup mounts the private source tree as a SYMLINK named private. .gitignore line 53 is the directory pattern `private/`, which does not match a symlink, and `git check-ignore -q private/` additionally exits 128 with "pathspec 'private/' is beyond a symbolic link". Nothing in the repository moved: the check was measuring the shape of the mount, not a repository change.
firstRun.whatWasChanged: The mount, not the check and not the repository. `private` was replaced by a real directory containing one symlink per child of the source tree (human-source-returns, source-imports, source-corpus-environment.txt). The repository's own committed .gitignore then ignores it on its own terms and `git ls-files private/` returns nothing, which is exactly the invariant the check states.

laneGate.separateFinding: A repository-local core.excludesFile is set in the shared .git/config of /home/user/captain-worktree, pointing at /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vf07-excludes, a file outside the repository whose only line is `private`. Every worktree of that repository inherits it. It happened to ignore the symlink, which is why the failure above was a near miss rather than a silent pass. This lane did not remove it: it is another lane's configuration in a shared repository config. Reported for whoever owns that checkout.
